tryThisNow: Open the next investment note and add a pair line before deciding: name the alternative claim on capital, then mark whether risk, quality, or price changes the first impression.

implementationPlan.title: Edit Your Pair Comparison Screen
implementationPlan.coreSkill: Before a candidate stays active, change the place where the decision is made: put a peer beside it, separate the industry label from actual risk, and make the valuation premium prove that the better business is still the better stock.

ifThenPlans.plan: If an email draft recommends a company by itself, then add a pair line naming the alternative claim on capital before sending it.
If a calendar block is set aside for two same-sector names, then start by marking leverage, assets, earnings stability, and management before treating the labels as comparable.
If the front desk note says the better business is the better stock, then add a price check asking whether the premium exceeds the quality difference.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Before tomorrow ends, edit one active investment note so it cannot stand alone: add a peer, add a risk line, and add a premium line that tests whether quality is being overcapitalized.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: Use a two-trigger checklist each week. Trigger one: any company judged alone gets a peer line. Trigger two: any superior business gets a premium line before it stays active.
